test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2023: Official Paper (Held On: 17 Aug, 2023 Shift 4)
subject: general
question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

A) in social evolution by imitation

B) by reason of its higher standard of living

C) the royal style is the agent

D) and cultural patterns are similarly transmitted by the dominant caste
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2** i.e. **'C,A,D,B.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence** begins **logically with **'C'**, stating that "the royal style is the agent", indicating the subject of the sentence. 
 
• The phrase **'A',** "in social evolution by imitation", follows 'C' to complete the idea introduced, indicating the manner in which the royal style acts as an agent.
 
• **'D', **"and cultural patterns are similarly transmitted by the dominant caste", builds on the statement by adding another layer of explanation on how not just the royal style but also cultural patterns are transmitted.
 
• **'B'**, "by reason of its higher standard of living", finally provides the reason why the royal style and cultural patterns are influential, tying the sentence together to make a coherent statement about social evolution.

Therefore, the** correct answer **is **Option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1** **(C, D, A, B)**: This arrangement doesn't flow logically because it suggests that cultural patterns transmitted by the dominant caste directly relate to social evolution by imitation, missing the crucial connection to the royal style being the agent.
 
• **Option 3 (B, C, D, A)**: Starting with 'B' makes the sentence awkward because it mentions the reason ("by reason of its higher standard of living") before stating what it is explaining, leading to confusion.
 
• **Option 4 (B, A, C, D)**: This arrangement fails because it begins with the reason before introducing the subject (the royal style), making the sentence structure illogical.
